# 4 Maccabees Chapter 7 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** Praise of Eleazar

---

**1** O blessed old age! O venerable white hair! O life that lived the law faithfully and was sealed in the honor of martyrdom!

**2** If old age had yielded in piety for a brief season and had been saved, many would have said that the piety of old age is hollow, that it saves its own skin.

**3** But Eleazar has made old age truly honored — not by shrinking but by standing firm and dying faithfully.

**4** He proved that in those who are devoted to piety, old age is truly beautiful and is not shamed by boldness in the face of danger but crowned by it.

**5** What is more wonderful — that reason was victorious over the passions in this man, or that the law through its instruction in him won this victory over the passions?

**6** Eleazar the priest, ninety years of age, his body already withered with old age, his flesh consumed by the torments, proved through the victory of holy reason that reason is master of the passions.

**7** O you who triumphed over the tyrant through the strength of your reasoning, and overcame every pain that the torturers inflicted!

**8** Just as Aaron our father, seizing the censer and running through the congregation in flames, overcame the fiery messenger by the power of reason,

**9** so too Eleazar, who was consumed in fire, showed by his willingness to die that reason empowered by devotion can quench every fire.

**10** Admirable also was this: although his body was already broken by age and his strength was diminished, he revived his youthful courage through reason and, with divine help, nullified the power of the rack.

**11** O noble father! O great elder! O holy guardian of the law! You did not tremble before the instruments of torture!

**12** You were not turned from your purpose by the whip! You were not conquered by the burning!

**13** You held firm in devotion to the holy name of God and remained faithful in piety until your last breath!

**14** O true priest of God, O faithful keeper of the sacred law, O guardian of religious devotion!

**15** Though your body was being consumed by fire, your soul clung to the sacred purpose of the law.

**16** Your courage and self-mastery proved beyond question that reason governs the passions.

**17** Even your enemies stood in awe as they saw you enduring their torments without yielding.

**18** Even the tyrant and all his council were astonished at your endurance.

**19** And this brought no small glory to your people and to the divine law.

**20** After Eleazar's death, the seven brothers were brought forward with their mother to undergo the same testing.

**21** These brothers had been reared in the same law and trained in the same devotion, and in every way they were worthy of the noble old priest.

**22** Their mother, beholding them all and rejoicing in this noble spirit within them, addressed them in their ancestral tongue: My children, the contest is noble, and God summons you to it for the testimony of our nation. Fight zealously for the law of our fathers.

**23** She added: It would be unreasonable for me, who gave birth to you and raised you to love your souls, to be overcome with grief at your deaths.
